title: Research report providers: Improving the quality of investment research
subject: This guide addresses the obligations of Australian financial services (AFS) licensees who provide research reports on investment products, including research analysts, securities analysts, and research houses. It focuses on improving the quality of investment research for retail and wholesale clients.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and provides guidance on licensing and conduct obligations in Part 7.7 of that Act as they apply to general advice prepared by research report providers. It is intended for AFS licensees who are research report providers, helping them meet their regulatory obligations.
ruling: ASIC expects research report providers to manage conflicts of interest and ensure the quality and transparency of their research. The guide outlines ASIC's interpretation of the law regarding the provision of general advice in research reports, including disclosure requirements and the need for robust research methodologies. ASIC states it will consider a provider's compliance with this guide when exercising its regulatory powers, such as surveillance and enforcement actions. The guide emphasizes that research reports must be fair, balanced, and not misleading, and providers should have adequate internal compliance procedures.
